parsed.study_design: Empirical implementation case study using community meetings, focus groups, interviews, observations, and technical measurements
parsed.population_and_sample: Residents and WASH stakeholders in Bashnet, Babati district (population 35,137), including women, community leaders, government and NGO personnel, and a specifically consulted group of 10 disabled residents (six women and four men); total participant numbers for most activities were not reported.
parsed.exposure: WaterAid's equity-and-inclusion approach to WASH planning and implementation, including inclusive consultation, partner capacity-building, accessible facility design, community participation, tariff reform, and representation on the local Water Board.
parsed.outcome: Water and sanitation access and exclusion outcomes, including accessibility of water points for disabled residents and women, affordability through reduced tariffs and free service for economically disadvantaged residents, participation in WASH decisions, and representation on the Water Board.
parsed.rationale: The Bashnet section identifies an implementation case study and reports information gathered from September 2010 to October 2011 through community meetings, focus groups, interviews, observations, and technical measurements (pp. 456–457). It empirically links the equity-and-inclusion intervention to access-relevant changes, including modified water-point designs, tariff reduction and free service for disadvantaged residents, improved physical accessibility, and inclusion of women and a disabled woman on the Water Board (pp. 461–463).
